metadata.title: From Page Swap to Bundle — the Retraction of Mode T
metadata.title_ja: ページ交代からバンドルへ——Mode T の撤回
participants: Tsuneo Ohnaka (大中庸生), architect and ruling authority
metadata.session_type: Evidence-driven retraction of a ratified design and its replacement

precedence: Register W v0.7, Register Map v0.3 and Deliverables 2-3 supersede all page-pair, CUR, Mode T and Mode W text of 2026-09-07
The customer's DP-5 (Mode T) and Appendix 5.A.2 +0xE row are superseded from the profile side (PR-5)
An agent finding both implements the bundle and flags the older text

rulings.ruling: Mode T retracted; bundle presentation adopted; PPM-1/PPM-2 RESTRICTED for packet blocks
STP, masked block copy (BCP), sweep-sequencer alias approved
g = 0 between consecutive Stays; Branch-0 wake within 4 clocks (1 clock or more is an investigation item)
OMIT CMT and RTW; RT.OUT at +0xE; WSV RESTRICTED (sequencer sole writer)
EW2 widened to N < N_MIN = 32; EW3-EW6 Error HALT
R2 (one packet body) preferred; R1 (unrolled) kept for bring-up; both selectable

reasoning_chain: Mode T: L1 reads the block named by CUR; per-packet CMT; program prepares packet b+1 during packet b; relied on F-F14 and 'rewrite only what changed'
Customer Hook A priced: CR5-L1 software clamp 35 instr with E8 at canonical edges vs STP 9; CR5-S1 conflicts with W-F1/W-T3 -> alias; CR5-I1 masked copy -> hardware BCP
Pricing the masked copy raised: into which page does it land, and does it survive the next swap?

F-F14 is literally true: untouched values are what the consumer was 'just' using - i.e. before the last commit; delta writes under a pointer flip are safe only across two windows (the back buffer is two frames old)
Model: Mode T correct at P=1, block stuck at P=2, wrong at P=3; per-sweep commit fixes [S] but a retune reverts every other sweep (partial settles halfway, wobbling at Fs/2)
Remedy (i) mirror to both pages: a straightforward two-pass rule failed 1,263/2,000; remedy (ii) single store + bundle + write windows: 0/2,000
L1 reads a block once per sample at packet start (CR3-B1/B2): protect the instant, not the interval; the latch is W-F22's staged/presented pair widened to eight values (customer's candidate b)
Construction: CUR alias writes only in the packet window; all blocks writable in housekeeping; sequencer prefetch; take-set at strobe; BCP in housekeeping; stay_value pin driven N/0
Fell away: CMT, RTW, WSV, E3, E7; the profile has no Q-band citizen, freeing the Core's single reservation slot for the packet re-entry
Found in the oracle: phase ADD must wrap -> W-F30

evidence.sweep_sim: 3 seeds x 20,000 samples; 215,627 packet plays; 4,174 GOs (1,175 full-load); 0 mismatches vs a reference from WPMS Ch.3/Ch.5 with the customer's step_toward; worst sweep 2,064/2,083 clocks
evidence.negative_tests: 13/13; mutant window (PH0 advanced twice) caught with 2,798 mismatches in 3,000 samples

pitfalls: A generator that stops generating looks like a clean run (null GO never cleared: 53 GOs in 12,000 samples)
A generator breaking the switch's sum-N rule exposed a missing backstop (2,899-clock sweeps) -> BCP re-checks the sweep in effect (EW5)
A failed hurried rule is not an impossibility proof for remedy (i)
Core timings in the oracle are nominal (wake 2, 4 per packet, 3 in housekeeping)
design_patterns: The Back Buffer Is Two Frames Old

upstream: W-D22 F-F14 consequence holds only for two-window differences
W-D23 name 大中恒夫 -> 大中庸生 in the CPU-Formation README
downstream: PR-1..PR-5 (sweep-word duplicates, N range, LE0 >= 0, paused-block reading of CR3-C1, +0xE wording and P <= 8 firm)

resumption_hooks: A: the Core score in Core syntax, R2 (preferred) and R1 (bring-up)
B: Layer 4 on DE10-nano - g, T_wake, N_MIN, BCP duration
C: master absorption of STP, BCP, bundle presentation; F-F14 restated
E: Claude Code generation of the sequencer and slot-major store with sweep_sim.py as golden model
closing_note: Protect the instant the consumer reads, not the time between.
